title: Improving Backward Conformal Prediction via Non-Conformity Score Transformation
claim: The baseline's estimated miscoverage is loose and far from the empirical value; our transformed estimator concentrates tightly near it across datasets.
layout: 3 panels in a row, KDE plots with dashed vertical reference lines
description: Three side-by-side kernel density plots, labeled (a) CIFAR-10 with T=2, (b) CIFAR-100 with T=20, and (c) Tiny-ImageNet with T=40. The x-axis is alpha and the y-axis is density. In each panel, a tall narrow green density (the proposed ST-BCP estimator) sits near zero. A wider blue density (the BCP baseline) sits far to the right. Dashed vertical lines mark the expectations of the two estimators (blue and green) and the true miscoverage (red). The green dashed line and the red dashed line almost overlap. The blue line is far from both. A legend in panel (a) explains the colors. The eye goes first to the large gap between the blue and green clusters. This shows that ours is much tighter to the empirical value.
caption: Performance comparison between BCP (h = s) and our method ST-BCP (h = Iw) under different datasets. We present kernel density estimation (KDE) plots of the LOO estimator, the empirical miscoverage, and the empirical expectation miscoverage level. All results are obtained using a ResNet50 model under the specified size constraint rule with a calibration set size n = 200. Note: Distributions that are more concentrated and closer to the empirical coverage indicate superior performance.
abstract: Conformal Prediction (CP) provides a statistical framework for uncertainty quantification that constructs prediction sets with coverage guarantees. While CP yields uncontrolled prediction set sizes, Backward Conformal Prediction (BCP) inverts this paradigm by enforcing a predefined upper bound on set size and estimating the resulting coverage guarantee. However, the looseness induced by Markov's inequality within the BCP framework causes a significant gap between the estimated coverage bound and the empirical coverage. In this work, we introduce ST-BCP, a novel method that introduces a data-dependent transformation of nonconformity scores to narrow the coverage gap. In particular, we develop a computable transformation and prove that it outperforms the baseline identity transformation. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, reducing the average coverage gap from 4.20\% to 1.12\% on common benchmarks.
